item.title: ASSAf publishes policy brief on air quality offsets as an air quality management instrument
item.description: A policy brief on air quality offsets as an instrument for air quality management in South Africa has been published under the auspices of the Academy of Science in South Africa (ASSAf). The brief explores the potential of air quality offsets to leverage resources and mitigate air pollution in historically neglected, predominantly low-income areas. item.title: Evaluation of atmospheric gaseous passive samplers through comparison with active in situ measurements
item.description: In order to assess compositional changes within the atmosphere it is crucial to measure concentrations of atmospheric trace gas species, which include the criteria pollutants sulphur dioxide (SO2), nitrogen dioxide (NO2) and ozone (O3). Measurement of these species with passive samplers is a generally acknowledged and frequently utilised method, which offers a cost-efficient sampling method to monitor these atmospheric species, especially, in data-scarce regions with logistical restraints. item.title: An assessment of ambient air quality in a densely populated urban settlement of Harare, Zimbabwe
item.description: Poor air quality in urban settings poses a significant global challenge with adverse environmental-health effects. In Zimbabwe, a critical knowledge gap exists regarding specific characteristics and seasonal variability of ambient air pollution in low-income, densely populated settlements, with existing studies often relying on indirect assessments. item.title: Vehicular exhaust emissions from road transport that substantially contribute to air pollution along Thika superhighway, Kenya
item.description: Road transportation is one of the anthropogenic sources of greenhouse gases (GHGs) and other air pollutants in Kenya, which have a serious negative impact on human health. item.title: Schmidt Number and its influence on turbulent energy dissipation in aeolian sand transport phenomena
item.description: This study examines the role of the turbulent Schmidt number (Sc) in shaping the dynamics of aeolian sand transport, with a particular focus on turbulent energy dissipation and particle diffusion. Using a mixture model framework and direct numerical simulations, we investigate both suspension (D = 2 μm) and saltation (D = 250 μm) modes under controlled wind tunnel conditions. item.title: Variation and health risks of the potentially toxic metals in dust around an industrial hub
item.description: The port area around Saldanha Bay, South Africa, is an industrial hub that processes large quantities of mining material and produces metals and steel, which leads to the visible emission of industrial dust. This study addresses the spatial and temporal variation of potentially toxic metals in the dust surrounding the industrial hub of Saldanha Bay and the potential health risks associated with them. item.title: Chemical Weather and Chemical Climate Conference brings together international experts to discuss state of air quality science in Africa
item.description: After the 1st Chemical Weather and Chemical Climate conference (CWCC) held in Shanghai in 2023, the 2nd CWCC conference was held at the University Mohammed VI Polytechnic (UM6P, https://cwcc2025-conference.org/) in Morocco during 14-16 October 2025.

item.title: CLEAN-Air Forum 2025: Fostering Africa-led partnerships for clean air solutions
item.description: The third edition of the CLEAN-Air Forum, held in Nairobi (Kenya) between 15-17 July 2025, under the theme of Partnerships for Clean Air Solutions, brought together more than 390 participants from more than 35 countries. The event was convened by the Nairobi County Government in partnership with the World Resources Institute-Africa, AirQo and the Health Effects Institute.
